top_papers.title: Personalized Affective Perception via Continual Learning in Human-Agent Negotiation
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes CLIFER, a continual learning method that allows negotiation agents to personalize their understanding of human emotions in real-time. By adapting to individual affective perception, the agent can adjust its negotiation strategy to achieve higher utility and elicit more concessions from human partners. The core contribution is a novel approach to real-time affective adaptation in human-agent negotiation, improving both agent performance and human experience.

top_papers.title: ProofCoder: Continuous Reasoning for Automated Software Verification
top_papers.abstract: ProofCoder is an agentic system for automated software verification that treats theorem proving as a continuous coding process. Unlike previous LLM approaches, it doesn't rely on a rigid tactic-generation loop. Instead, ProofCoder iteratively constructs, repairs, and refines proofs by continuously reasoning and using proof assistant feedback to dynamically decide on actions like gathering information, inspecting states, or backtracking.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1 . Overview of ProofCoder’s workflow.

top_papers.title: Quantifying the Sampling Frequency Invariance of Time-Series Foundation Models for Sensor Data Applications
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel method to evaluate the sampling frequency (SF) invariance of Time-Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) for sensor data. It quantifies how TSFMs' performance degrades with varying SFs, demonstrating that this degradation is linked to the loss of information bandwidth rather than the SF value itself. The study's key contribution is establishing SF-invariance as a critical evaluation metric for TSFMs in real-world sensor applications.
top_papers.figure_caption: TSFM embeddings on CWRU vibration data remain stable up to a 40% reduction in SF, but shift sharply between 40% and 50%. In this paper, we study and quantify these behavioral shifts across TSFM embeddings, forecasts, and downstream performance.

top_papers.title: AnalogLayoutWorld: An Open Benchmark for Agentic Analog Layout Design
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces **AnalogLayoutWorld**, an open benchmark designed to evaluate the capabilities of AI agents in analog circuit layout design. The benchmark provides a realistic environment with expert-reviewed tasks, integrated design tools, and comprehensive verification, addressing the challenges of long-horizon engineering tasks with physical constraints. Its core contribution is establishing a standardized platform for developing and assessing agents in this complex domain, revealing current agent performance and highlighting areas for improvement.
top_papers.figure_caption: Agentic analog layout design process. (a) A fixed netlist, specifications, and process design kit define the task. (b) The agent constructs and refines layouts using layout tools and verification feedback. (c) Integration, fabrication, and silicon characterization provide physical validation.

top_papers.title: Auditing AI peer reviewers: a benchmark on real scientific papers
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a benchmark for evaluating AI peer reviewers by injecting specific, localized errors into real scientific papers. The benchmark measures reviewers' ability to detect these errors across different types and severities, alongside their false-positive rates. The authors also present "Skepthical," a multi-agent reviewer designed to verify claims using external tools, and demonstrate its performance against other AI reviewers on astrophysics and ML preprints.

top_papers.title: Cortex-FL: Agent-Mediated Collaboration for Federated Learning
top_papers.abstract: Cortex-FL introduces an agent-native approach to federated learning, allowing users to specify learning goals in natural language. Its core method involves agents that automatically discover collaborators, define tasks, and manage incentives, streamlining the complex process of setting up and executing federated learning. The system's main contribution is enabling organizations without specialized expertise to easily participate in federated learning by abstracting away the coordination overhead while preserving data and computational control.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. From (a) agentic service delegation and (b) manually coordinated FL to (c) agent-mediated FL in Cortex-FL . Three panels compare coordination workflows. Panel (a) shows an agent delegating a software task to agents, tools, and services through A2A and MCP, with x402 payments. Panel (b) shows an organizer coordinating data owners through questions about participants, learning objectives, infrastructure, and incentives. Panel (c) shows CortexFL agentic nodes on AgentaNet coordinating a classifier for cats, dogs, birds, ships, and trucks through agreements, isolated training, and incentives.

top_papers.title: From Delegation to Coordination: Learning Efficient Multi-Agent Deep Research
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces LEAD-RL, a novel multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for deep research. Its core method is a joint training approach with contribution-aware credit assignment, where subagent reports are evaluated for their research utility to gate their rewards. The main contribution is improved answer quality across benchmarks by ensuring subagents provide reliable evidence, overcoming limitations of existing delegation methods.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of LEAD-RL . (a) The efficient delegation harness combines dynamic task routing with local and global verification. (b) Contribution-aware RL filters team-level outcome credit using subagent report judgments and jointly updates the main agent and subagents.
